newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak VSZ says interested in raising bank stake.
newsitem.headline: Slovak VSZ says interested in raising bank stake.

text.p: Slovak steel maker VSZ a.s. on Wednesday said it is interested in increasing its stake in bank IRB a.s. to as much as 40 percent from its reported stake of some 20 percent.

"Our first step is to get capital participation in IRB of over 20-30 percent, let's say 40 percent...Now is the time for pioneers and there are not that many companies that can do ," VSZ Director Jan Smerek told an industrial and economic conference.
VSZ's holdings in IRB caused a stir when it was recently revealed that it may have exceeded 15 percent, which by law needs central bank approval.
In August, VSZ asked for central bank permission to increase its stake in IRB, the third largest Slovak commercial bank, to over 20 percent.

Shortly after the request was filed, the Central Securities Registry (SCP) published figures showing VSZ already held some 20 percent of IRB, but later retracted the figures without further explanation.
On Tuesday, the central bank said it would reject the request on technical grounds, but has yet to officially do so.

Smerek said that central bank approval "would make the whole situation at the bank more transparent" and added that there were ways for VSZ to attain its goals even if did not have the central bank's blessing.
"There are other ways, other forms of getting the 40 percent," he said without elaborating.
"Our goal with capital participation in the bank is to help the flow of money, trading and financing of our consortium, it's good to have the bank 'closer'," he said.
"Unfortunately our financial institutions have so far not been able to do that with us," he added.
VSZ is a major client of IRB, accounting for an estimated 1.5 percent of the bank's total loan portfolio.
